In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution (ii) assert that the algorithm provably converges (a.s.) to the W2-barycenter of general non-parametric measures. Theorem thm: fixedpoint-convergence only establishes W2-precompactness and that every accumulation point is a fixed point of G; convergence to the barycenter is obtained only under the extra hypothesis that G has a unique fixed point, which the paper itself acknowledges fails in general (Example 3.1 of Álvarez-Esteban et al.) and is an open problem for non-parametric inputs. The prose therefore promises a guarantee the formal results do not deliver.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract/contributions to say the iterates are a.s. W2-precompact with all accumulation points being fixed points of G, and that convergence to the barycenter holds when G has a unique fixed point.
issues.overall_effect: The headline guarantee (a.s. convergence to the barycenter) is only conditional; for the advertised class of general non-parametric measures the established guarantee is subsequential convergence to fixed points of G.
issues.title: Unconditional convergence to the barycenter claimed, but theorem only gives fixed points of G unless G has a unique fixed point
issues.why_classification: No proof changes are required, but the advertised guarantee must be weakened to a conditional statement; a recognizably comparable (conditional) result survives, matching the deterministic scheme it extends.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the theorem takes conditional expectations given F_t and applies Markov/Borel–Cantelli to quantities defined through R̂_t = r̄_{1,2}(ρ̂_t,…) and N̂_{t,k} = n̄(μ̂_t,ν_k,…). For these to be F_t-measurable random variables, r̄_1, r̄_2 (Lemma lem: truncation-choice) and n̄, θ̃ (Proposition prop: OTmap-estimator-entropic) must depend measurably on the (random) measure argument. Lemma lem: truncation-choice only asserts existence of r̄_1, r̄_2 'that depend on ρ' with no measurability, and Proposition prop: OTmap-estimator-entropic (iii) defines n̄ via existence constants C_entr(μ,ν), θ̄(μ,ν) from a cited theorem without verifying the Borel dependence that Assumption asp: OTmap-estimator (iii) requires; no σ-algebra/topology on M^q(R^d) is even specified. Setting sett: convergence's 'Note that R̂_t is F_t-measurable' is thus unsupported.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix a σ-algebra on the relevant classes of measures, define r̄_1, r̄_2, n̄ as minimal integers satisfying the respective bounds, and verify (or assume) that the resulting maps are measurable; alternatively add a standing assumption that Borel selections exist.
issues.overall_effect: The filtered-probability-space construction and the conditional-expectation steps in the convergence proof rest on an unverified measurability premise; the conclusion is very likely true but the argument has a gap.

issues.why_classification: A routine, local measurability verification (or an explicit standing assumption) closes the gap without changing any conclusion, method, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Statement (iii) asserts E‖T̂_entr[θ]−T‖² ≤ C[θ^{-d/2}(log(n)n^{-1/2}+log(m)m^{-1/2})+θ^{ᾱ/2}] for all m ≥ m̲ = 1 and n ≥ n̲ = d+1. The proof derives the cited bound only for m,n ≥ 2 and the simplified form only for m,n ≥ 7 (needed for monotonicity of log x/√x). For m = 1 the term log(m)m^{-1/2} vanishes, so the displayed bound would force the error to be controlled by the n- and θ-terms alone; but with a single sample from μ the Sinkhorn potentials ĝ_j are determined by X_1 alone and T̂ carries no information about μ, so the bound cannot hold as stated. The claimed range of validity exceeds what is proven.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the displayed bound in (iii) to m, n ≥ 7 (or ≥ max{7, d+1}), matching the proof.
issues.overall_effect: Only the first display of statement (iii) is affected; the 'in particular' part (with n̄ ≥ 7) and all downstream uses remain valid.
issues.title: Consistency bound in Proposition (iii) stated for all m ≥ 1, n ≥ d+1 but only proven (and only plausible) for m, n ≥ 7
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of the quantifier range fixes the mismatch; the consistency conclusion actually used (via n̄ ≥ 7) is unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: Tractability (Remark remark: computational-tractability) is argued for Algorithm algo: iteration with arbitrary user-chosen R̂_t, N̂_{t,k}, Θ̂_{t,k}, while convergence (Theorem thm: fixedpoint-convergence, Corollary cor: fixedpoint-convergence-entropic) is proven only under Setting sett: convergence, whose choices N̂_{t,k} = n̄(μ̂_t,ν_k,ε) and R̂_t = r̄_{1,2}(ρ̂_t,…) require the non-explicit existence constants C_entr(μ̂_t,ν_k), θ̄(μ̂_t,ν_k), ᾱ from the cited Pooladian–Niles-Weed theorems (depending on the unknown Brenier potential of the current random iterate) and tail-moment thresholds of ρ̂_t. These are not computable from samples, so the schedule that carries the guarantee is an oracle schedule; the implemented algorithm (parameters chosen heuristically, per the GitHub reference) carries no proven guarantee. The prose conflates the two.

failure_location.quote: Consequently, using $\widehat{T}_{\mathrm{entr}}[\theta]$ as the OT map estimator in Algorithm~\ref{algo: iteration} results in a computationally tractable and efficient algorithm for Wasserstein barycenter that is also provably convergent.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State explicitly that the convergence guarantee holds for a parameter schedule defined through non-explicit problem-dependent constants (an existence result for a convergent schedule), and that the implemented tractable version uses heuristic parameters not covered by the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The joint claim 'computationally tractable and provably convergent' is not established for any single implementable specification of the algorithm; the guarantee is for an idealized schedule and the tractability for the unguaranteed heuristic version.
issues.title: Claim of a computationally tractable and provably convergent algorithm: the convergent parameter schedule depends on non-computable oracle quantities
issues.why_classification: No formal result is false, but the advertised combined guarantee must be weakened to an existence-of-schedule statement, a limited but real loss of the promised practical guarantee.
